import importlib.util, os, shutil
for name in ('fitz', 'pypdf', 'pdfplumber', 'PIL', 'pypdfium2'):
    print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))

    print(name, shutil.which(name))
print(os.listdir('/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/utility/.runtime/ghostscript-9.55.0'))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:',reader.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
    texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n{text}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts)[:36000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
scratch=Path('tmp/pdfs')
files=[scratch/'manuscript.txt',scratch/'page-07-detail.png']
files += [scratch/f'page-{i:02d}.{ext}' for i in range(1,17) for ext in ('txt','png')]
for path in files:
    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
for path in (scratch, scratch.parent):
    if path.is_dir() and not any(path.iterdir()):
        path.rmdir()
print('Removed review scratch files; manuscript unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: The architecture offers a potentially useful combination of persistent low-dimensional memory, competition among patches across a batch, and associative retrieval. Integrating this workspace into a ViT provides a concrete approach to studying memory-guided visual representations.

The matched ViT comparisons provide meaningful evidence of benefit. In Table 1, AiT-Small improves CIFAR-10 accuracy from 79.53% to 83.34% and CIFAR-100 from 53.19% to 56.30%, with parameters increasing from 14.9M to 15.8M. Both gains also persist, although more modestly, for the Base models.

Table 2 includes useful component ablations. Removing the bottleneck reduces CIFAR-10 accuracy from 83.34% to 75.40%, while replacing Hopfield retrieval with cross-attention reduces it to 81.03%. These results support the utility of the combined design under the reported training conditions.

The memory-initialization experiments, inverse-temperature sweep, attention visualizations, and energy measurements help characterize the architecture beyond aggregate accuracy. The single-layer comparisons in Figure 4 also demonstrate a favorable parameter–accuracy tradeoff against Coordination.
weaknesses: The inference protocol is materially underspecified. Section 4.1 explicitly mixes patches across training samples, and Equation 4 maintains memory over time, but evaluation-time updates, memory resets, and batch composition are not described. If updates continue during evaluation, predictions can depend on other test inputs and their order. Behavior with small batches is also unclear: the CIFAR bottleneck selects 512 patches, whereas one image provides only 64. These omissions prevent a clear assessment of reproducibility and conventional per-image inference.

The central complexity claims do not follow from the equations. Bottleneck attention first computes dense M-by-(BN) scores, costing O(BNMD) per head before top-k selection. Input projections and retrieval introduce further input-dependent work, and the full architecture retains quadratic within-image self-attention. A fixed memory bank therefore does not establish complexity invariance to input quantity or dimension. Parameter counts alone, without compute, latency, or peak-memory measurements, do not substantiate the broader efficiency claims.

The load component of the balance loss is problematic as written. Equation 5 counts positive entries of A, which was defined as softmax attention and is therefore positive everywhere mathematically. If masked attention is intended instead, the hard counts have zero gradients almost everywhere, and no surrogate estimator is specified. The importance component can still provide gradients, but the claimed contribution of the complete loss is not established. Figures 8–9 show training progression rather than a controlled comparison with the loss removed.

The Hopfield reader is insufficiently specified and its distinction from attention is overstated. Equations 7–8 provide an energy and an argmin without an initialized retrieval algorithm, iteration count, stopping criterion, or differentiation procedure. For the stated energy, the standard fixed-point update is softmax attention with tied keys and values. The contribution can therefore lie in its integration and parameterization, but the claimed fundamental departure from attention is misleading. Section 2's assertion that previous latent methods require equal input and memory dimensions also conflicts with Table 5's Perceiver entries.

The evidence supports a narrower performance claim than the manuscript makes. On relational Sort-of-CLEVR, AiT reaches 67.74%, below Coordination's 73.43% and CNN+RN's 81.07% (Table 4); Triangle performance essentially matches ViT. Different parameter budgets and limited baseline-tuning details also weaken broader superiority claims. These results do not erase the CIFAR gains, but they leave the proposed advantage for relational association incompletely supported.

Secondary reporting issues include inconsistent learning rates between Section 5.1 (1e-5) and Table 6 (1e-4), an unspecified validation procedure for grid search, and missing variability estimates alongside the main three-run averages. These are correctable; the weak-reject recommendation is driven primarily by the unresolved inference protocol, mathematical specification, and unsupported complexity claims.
